# Active work — lege-docwrite

Live work, grouped by parent in `ROADMAP.md` order. Blocked work names its blocker inline.

## [M7 — images, bidi, IDML spreads, CFF and PDF links](ROADMAP.md#m7--images-bidi-idml-spreads-cff-and-pdf-links) `@docwrite.milestone.m7-open-items/1`

### Right-to-left and mixed-direction text

`proposed` · `@docwrite.work.m7-bidi/1` · part of `@docwrite.milestone.m7-open-items/1`

unicode-bidi is a dependency but paragraphs are shaped left to right; resolve embedding levels, shape runs in their direction and reorder lines for display, caret and PDF.

### EPUB export, if it proves useful

`proposed` · `@docwrite.work.m7-epub/1` · part of `@docwrite.milestone.m7-open-items/1`

Markdown and PDF cover the semantic and print paths; an EPUB 3 package from the same blocks and styles is optional.

### IDML with spreads and threaded text frames

`proposed` · `@docwrite.work.m7-idml-spreads/1` · part of `@docwrite.milestone.m7-open-items/1`

export_idml writes a design map, styles, one master spread and the story, but no spreads or text frames, so InDesign has nowhere to flow the story; emit spreads per page pair with threaded frames on the master's text area. Not yet opened in InDesign.

### Place images in the page flow

`proposed` · `@docwrite.work.m7-images/1` · part of `@docwrite.milestone.m7-open-items/1`

Image blocks lay out as text today; read the asset's size, place it full-measure or inline with its caption kept with it, draw it on screen and embed it in the PDF (JPEG/PNG through lege-pdf-write).

### PDF link annotations and named destinations

`proposed` · `@docwrite.work.m7-pdf-links/1` · part of `@docwrite.milestone.m7-open-items/1`

Links and citations are plain text in the PDF; add link annotations (URIs, and internal destinations for contents, index and citations) to lege-pdf-write and use them.

## Unparented

### DjVu reader backend behind document engine

`proposed` · `@docwrite.work.djvu-reader/1`

Add a DjVu reader backend after the common reader surface is host-independent.
Keep the document descriptor, cancellation and worker contract format-neutral:
normalize page geometry at the engine boundary and advertise optional text,
outline, link and progressive-pass capabilities. Image-only pages must work
without fabricated text artifacts. Preserve bounded worker and memory use
when a PDF and DjVu document are both open. The current djvulibrust crate
in Lege-ecosystem is an encoder, so identify a decoder and measure its
licensing and performance before selecting it.

### Shared command registry and platform menu adapters

`proposed` · `@docwrite.work.liminaldoc-native-menus/1`

Prepare one semantic command registry for Liminaldoc with stable command IDs,
labels, accelerators, enabled and checked state, and dispatch against the
active document surface. The same definitions should feed keyboard shortcuts,
compact in-window controls, and future native menus. Separate manuscript
Save (the editable .legebook) from Save As/Export of derivatives without
duplicating file commands. Host-thread ownership must govern menu updates.

Implement platform adapters later: macOS application and window menus via
native APIs, a PixelKit-drawn menu for Linux with optional desktop
integration, and a Windows adapter using winsafe where its API is suitable.
The EvidenceIntake repository named by the user could not be inspected at
this URL during scoping, so its approach is a lead to verify, not authority.
No native menu integration is included in the extraction work.

### PDF document tab alongside manuscript tabs

`proposed` · `@docwrite.work.pdf-document-tab/1`

After the manuscript New/Open/Save and writing-ready paths are reliable, add a
PDF tab alongside editable document tabs. A PDF tab keeps its own page position,
zoom, search and selection, and routes keyboard, pointer, scroll and IME input
only to the active surface. Reuse the Lege PDF engine and viewer behaviour by
extracting a host-independent PDF view/controller; do not embed ViewerApp's
separate winit event loop or treat a source pane as the PDF tab.

### Optional SymSpell spellchecking behind a feature flag

`proposed` · `@docwrite.work.spellcheck-optional/1`

Add optional, off-by-default spellchecking to the writer: SymSpell (symspell 0.5.x, MIT, pure Rust) behind a `spellcheck` cargo feature in a new docwrite-spell crate, run as a debounced per-paragraph background job that never touches the keypress-to-present path.

### lege-pdf-write: subset and embed TrueType and CFF fonts

`proposed` · `@lege.work.font-subsetting-and-cff/1`

Subset fonts to the glyphs used (e.g. the subsetter crate) and embed both FontFile2 TrueType and FontFile3 CFF/OpenType programs with correct widths and descriptors.

### lege-pdf-write: links, named destinations and page labels

`proposed` · `@lege.work.links-labels-destinations/1`

Add link annotations (internal and URI), named destinations for chapters/notes, page labels (roman front matter, arabic body), and streaming finalize without a fixed page count.

### lege-pdf-write: path operators, RGB fill and Flate images

`proposed` · `@lege.work.vector-paths-and-color/1`

Add path construction/stroke/fill operators and RGB colour for rules, underlines and ornaments, and Flate-compressed RGB/alpha images with SMask.

### Optional damage rectangles through the presenter

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.work.damage-rects/1`

Let render report damaged rectangles and let presenters use them (softbuffer present_with_damage), keeping full-frame repaint as the default.

### PixelKit raster SIMD coverage with scalar equivalence

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.work.raster-simd-coverage/1`

Expand PixelKit raster SIMD coverage where profiles justify it, beginning
with exact max-coverage spans and then identity-size opaque bitmap rows.
Preserve byte-for-byte scalar results, clipped tails and alpha endpoints
on x86_64 and aarch64; retain a portable fallback. Benchmark both short
glyph spans and long rows before accepting a vector path. Consider damage
rectangles and idle wakeup behavior before vectorizing whole-frame work.
